li.label: a name for mercy
li.description: A traveler had heard we spare the ones we beat. Strange thing to be famous for. I'll take it.

li.label: known as soft
li.description: On the road they say we patch up raiders and send them home. They're laughing at us out there, and they're right to.

li.label: a kindness came back
li.description: We let someone go once. Today a trader remembered it and paid us back in herbs and coin. Mercy travels.

li.label: they fear us
li.description: A visitor pulled a child away from me today. I was only going to wave.

li.label: feared on the road
li.description: The visitors keep their children close when I walk by. Good. Let them.

li.label: frightened a trader
li.description: The trader gave us a better price because they were afraid of us. The silver spends the same. It still doesn't sit right.

li.label: a frightened trader's price
li.description: Didn't even have to haggle. The trader just kept lowering the price. A name is worth something after all.

li.label: fed a traveler
li.description: A stranger came out of their way because they'd heard we'd feed them. We did. Twice.

li.label: another mouth at the door
li.description: Every hungry traveler on the road knows where our kitchen is now. Wonderful.

li.label: spoken well of
li.description: Folk on the road still talk about what we gave away. I like being that kind of place.

li.label: known for hard bargains
li.description: The trader expected a fight over every coin, and got one. Our name is worth more than their margins.

li.label: called a miser
li.description: A trader haggled with me like I was a known cheat. Apparently we count every grain. Apparently that's what we're known for.

li.label: proved a point
li.description: A guest brought their own bread because they'd heard we wouldn't share. I shared. Out of spite, mostly, but I shared.

li.label: our ways praised
li.description: An old traveler said we keep the old customs better than anywhere on the road. Good to know they aren't wasted on us.

li.label: a guest who knew our ways
li.description: The trader waited for the bread and salt at the gate, the proper way. Small thing. Felt like being understood.

li.label: showed off our new ideas
li.description: A traveler came all this way to see what we're trying. I talked for an hour. I could have talked for three.

li.label: nothing where it was
li.description: The trader couldn't find the storeroom because we moved it again. I suppose that's what we're like now. I suppose I like it.

li.label: guests at ease
li.description: The visitors took their boots off and sang with us half the night. That's what a welcome is for.

li.label: trusted with the road's news
li.description: The trader told me things they don't tell everyone, because we always let them in. It pays to keep the gate open.

li.label: guests afraid to move
li.description: A visitor asked my leave to walk to the well. Is that what we are now? The place where you ask before you breathe?

li.label: guests minding their manners
li.description: The visitors kept their hands where we could see them. Good. That's how it should be.

li.label: opened the gate a little
li.description: I let a trader in past the watch instead of haggling through a crack. The sky didn't fall. Imagine that.

li.label: the work was noticed
li.description: A trader stood and stared at our fields. Not a weed. People on the road know what we do here.

li.label: an idle hour
li.description: A visitor made me sit down. Just sit. I'd forgotten how. I should do it again sometime. Next year, maybe.

li.label: the envy of travelers
li.description: A stranger looked at how we live and wanted it. Long lunches, no bells, nobody counting. We've got something good here.

li.label: thought idle
li.description: Travelers think we're the place where nobody works. I work. I'd like that noted somewhere.

li.label: no hurry
li.description: A trader waited on us, and nobody died of it. Things here happen when they happen.

li.label: kept a trader waiting
li.description: A trader waited half a day for us to wake up. Half a day! I'd have had the deal done and a fence mended.

li.label: gave someone sanctuary
li.description: They came to us because they'd heard we were merciful. We were. I'd like to keep being.

li.label: we took in a runaway
li.description: Someone ran from their own people to us, and we didn't send them back. That's who I want us to be.

li.label: gave a runaway back
li.description: They trusted me with what they wanted. The council handed it straight to the people they were running from.

li.label: we gave them up
li.description: We told their masters what they'd asked of us. Somewhere on the road, someone is paying for having trusted this place.

li.label: betrayed to my own people
li.description: I asked them for help. They went and told the one person I was hiding from. Merciful, they said. Merciful.

li.label: a night's rest
li.description: They couldn't keep me. They gave me a warm corner and a full bowl anyway. It'll carry me a while.

li.label: sent them back on the road
li.description: A night's rest and a full bowl. It was kind. It wasn't what they asked for.

li.label: not so soft after all
li.description: I heard this place was soft. The new guard on my door didn't get the message.

li.label: nobody's fool
li.description: The prisoner thought our mercy meant weakness. Found out otherwise.

li.label: hard on a prisoner
li.description: One prisoner made a joke about our mercy, so we took it away from them. That's not what mercy is for.

li.label: taken for fools
li.description: The prisoner laughed at our mercy, and the council opened the door anyway. I hope it was worth it.

li.label: mercy sent out
li.description: We sent food to people who were afraid of us, and asked nothing back. Maybe the stories will change. Maybe I'll sleep.

li.label: gone soft
li.description: We're going easy on people who used to fear us. Fear kept the walls standing.

li.label: silver instead
li.description: The council sent silver, not food. It's something. It's not quite what I asked for.

li.label: still the place they fear
li.description: I asked for one kind thing. The council said our name is doing its job.

li.label: known for cruelty
li.description: They use our name to frighten children. The council seems content with that. I'm not.

li.label: flogged by strangers
li.description: My own people handed me to strangers to be whipped, because these strangers have a name for it. My back will remember their yard.

li.label: held the whip
li.description: That one held the whip. I made sure to learn the face.

li.label: held the whip
li.description: The visitors asked for me by name, because of what we're known for. I did it. I can still hear it.

li.label: kept our name
li.description: They came all this way to see us do it properly. We did. People will remember.

li.label: a flogging in our yard
li.description: We whipped somebody else's thief because they asked us to. Our name has turned into a service we offer.

li.label: spared by strangers
li.description: My own people wanted me whipped. The hard ones, the ones from the stories, untied my hands instead.

li.label: could have, didn't
li.description: They had the whip in hand and every excuse to use it. They didn't.

li.label: put the whip down
li.description: They handed me a whip and a name to live up to. The council said no. I didn't know how much I wanted it to.

li.label: nobody turned away
li.description: Hungry at our gate, fed at our table. Every time. I'm proud of that, even when the larder isn't.

li.label: feeding the whole road
li.description: Every hungry mouth for three valleys knows the way to our kitchen. Our winter is going out the gate one bowl at a time.

li.label: food for work
li.description: Anyone who wants a bowl splits wood first. Fair's fair, and the woodpile looks wonderful.

li.label: the gate closed to the hungry
li.description: We used to be the place with the full pot. Now we're the place with the closed gate.

li.label: no more handouts
li.description: The food we grow stays with the people who grow it. About time.

li.label: an unexpected gift
li.description: Their lot are supposed to be misers. Then this one sent me off with a full purse. Hm.

li.label: saved face
li.description: The trader called us misers. We sent them off with a gift they'll be talking about for a month. Let them talk about that.

li.label: silver for a joke
li.description: We paid a trader to stop laughing at us. Most expensive joke I've ever heard.

li.label: laughed at for our thrift
li.description: A trader made fools of us in front of everyone, and the council let it stand. My ears burned for an hour.

li.label: thrifty and proud
li.description: Let them laugh. Our silver stays where it is, and theirs doesn't.

li.label: charged me for water
li.description: Two silver a bucket. I made a joke, and they turned it into a price list.

li.label: made it worse
li.description: I asked the council to shut the trader up. They charged for water instead. Now the whole road has a new story about us.

li.label: made to keep the custom
li.description: The council ordered me to keep a custom I don't believe in. So I keep it. Loudly, and badly.

li.label: the custom upheld
li.description: Some things here are older than any of us, and the council remembered that.

li.label: free to choose
li.description: The council said I can keep the custom or not, as I like. Funny: now I'm half tempted to keep it.

li.label: the custom slighted
li.description: The council decided our customs are optional now. I wonder what else will turn out to be optional.

li.label: an old custom brought back
li.description: We did it the old way again, all of us at one table. I'd forgotten how much I missed it.

li.label: brought it back
li.description: I asked for one old thing to be kept, and the council said yes. For an evening it felt like home again.

li.label: an old custom, new again
li.description: We brought back the old evening, with a few new twists of course. It's us, after all.

li.label: not quite how it was
li.description: They brought it back, sort of. It's different now. Better than nothing. Mostly.

li.label: the old ways let go
li.description: The council said we've outgrown it. Maybe we have. I hadn't.

li.label: a guest in my bed
li.description: The council says guests are guests. My guest is in my bed, my boots and my beer.

li.label: made welcome
li.description: These people never tell you to go. I could get used to this. I have.

li.label: the guest earned their keep
li.description: We handed our guest an axe. Living like family means working like family. The woodpile agrees.

li.label: got my bed back
li.description: The guests were shown the road and I got my bed back. It smells of someone else, but it's mine.

li.label: had me shown out
li.description: They're supposed to be the friendly ones. This one had me walked to the edge of their land.

li.label: guests sent off
li.description: We walked a whole party of guests to the edge of the map because one of them borrowed some boots.

li.label: my old friend let in
li.description: The council opened the gate for my old friend. We ate at the same table, like before. I won't forget it.

li.label: let in at last
li.description: They don't let strangers in. They let me in. My old friend must have begged.

li.label: the rules bent
li.description: The council let a stranger in because someone asked nicely. So much for the rules.

li.label: my friend kept outside
li.description: My oldest friend slept outside the walls with the pack animals, because rules are rules. I passed a blanket over the wall like a thief.

li.label: kept outside the walls
li.description: My friend lives behind those walls, and I slept outside them with the mules.

li.label: a night outside the walls
li.description: The gate stayed shut, so I went out through it. We talked until the fire was ash. Worth every yawn.

li.label: a day off
li.description: The council gave me a day. I sat by the water and did nothing, and nobody counted. I'd forgotten what that feels like.

li.label: a day of rest
li.description: A whole day with no work, for everyone. The fields kept. Turns out we do too.

li.label: a wasted day
li.description: A whole day without work. I sat on my hands and counted everything that wasn't getting done.

li.label: worked ragged
li.description: I asked for one day. The work won't wait, they said. Neither, it turns out, will I.

li.label: the council backed me
li.description: Everyone pulls their weight now, by order. Took long enough. My back thanks the council.

li.label: put to work
li.description: The council says everyone pulls their weight now. Mine was resting. It liked resting.

li.label: about time
li.description: Finally, everyone pulling their weight. I might even get a full night's sleep.

li.label: thanked in front of everyone
li.description: They stood up at supper and thanked me by name. Nobody's lifting any more than before, but now they know who has been.

li.label: told to slow down
li.description: I said I was carrying everyone. The council told me to stop carrying. That's not how fields work.
